payload.title: GDX: the weekly low window opens, then a confirmed weekly cycle low; void if the window closes first
payload.context: I am waiting for GDX's weekly cycle low inside its weekly low window. There is no price that would prove me wrong, only time: if the window closes without a confirmed weekly low, the idea is void.
payload.nextStep: When the weekly low confirms, review the trade against it.

conditions.label: Next confirmed weekly cycle low (any price)

invalidation.label: Void if no confirmed weekly low before the weekly low window closes

explanation:
I'd first send this as a dry run. That saves nothing. DWLF restates each condition in plain words, and I'd show you that before saving it for real (the same payload without dryRun).

What DWLF will check, once a night after the US close, using end-of-day data only:
1. Step 1: GDX's weekly low window opens. This is the window DWLF's engine draws for the next weekly cycle low. You'll get an alert when it opens: a Telegram digest if you've set one up, an in-app notification, and the Theses page.
2. Step 2: this is checked only after step 1 is met. It's the next confirmed weekly cycle low on GDX, at any price, because you gave no level. A weekly low is confirmed some bars after its low week, and every alert says when DWLF could first know it.
3. The void: you asked for this, so I added it. DWLF uses the stored weekly low window, measured from GDX's last weekly low on the day you save. If that window's last week ends and no weekly cycle low has been confirmed since you saved, the thesis is marked challenged. You then decide whether to keep, revise or close it.

What it won't do:
- It won't give you advice or forecasts. It reports what happened; it doesn't say what to trade or expect.
- It doesn't watch intraday.
- It doesn't invent a stop price. You have none, so the thesis has no price invalidation.
- Nothing that happened before you save counts.
- It doesn't close your idea for you. A challenged thesis waits for your answer.
- The void is strict. A low confirmed after the window has closed doesn't save it, even if the low week itself falls inside the window.
- The void is not decided the day the window closes. DWLF waits 28 days after the closing week, so a late confirmation can't slip in.
- Step 2 doesn't check that the low is dated inside the window. It's met by the next confirmed weekly low after the window opens. The void is what covers 'no low by the close'.
- If a weekly low confirms before the window even opens, the void no longer applies. DWLF draws a new window from that low, and step 1 then waits for the new window.

I can't give you the window's dates yet. DWLF returns them on save, or with the save refused if there's no stored window or it has already closed. After that, 'how close' shows the opening week, the closing week and the days left.
